title: Independent Canonical Documents
summary: explain how Docs Viewer source can be seeded from another canonical system and then remain independently canonical without synchronization
content_html:
Independent Canonical Documents

Purpose

Docs Viewer can own canonical documents and document relationships whose initial identity or content came from canonical data in another application. Creation establishes a new Docs Viewer source; it does not establish an ongoing replica.

This lets Studio remain canonical for structured records while Docs Viewer becomes canonical for the documents that explain, interpret, or refer to those records.

Mental Model

Studio canonical record
    -> optional creation-time validation and one-time seed
    -> canonical Docs Viewer source

Studio record -------------------- independent later lifecycle
Docs Viewer source --------------- independent later lifecycle

optional cross-application identity
    -> may resolve
    -> may become stale
    -> is diagnosed or repaired by its owning workflow

Canonical ownership is contextual rather than global:

  • Studio JSON is canonical for the Studio record.
  • Docs Viewer Markdown/front matter is canonical for the document.
  • Generated document payloads, public projections, search indexes, reports, and usage indexes are rebuildable projections of their owning source.

Calling the document canonical does not make it authoritative for the Studio record, and calling the Studio record canonical does not make the document a generated cache.

One-Time Seeding Is Not Synchronization

A producing workflow may:

  • allocate a stable document identity;
  • create a source document from selected record fields;
  • validate the initial association;
  • store a one-way document reference; and
  • rebuild the resulting Docs Viewer projections.

After creation:

  • editing the Studio record does not edit the document;
  • editing the document does not edit the Studio record;
  • deleting the Studio record does not delete the document;
  • deleting the document does not edit the Studio record; and
  • neither side infers a replacement from title, content, or other mutable data.

A later workflow may offer explicit inspection or repair, but repair is a user action over an acknowledged stale relationship. It is not background synchronization.

Structural Validation And Tolerant References

Docs Viewer validates the contracts it owns:

  • source and front-matter structure;
  • identity shape and configured collection confinement;
  • token or reference syntax;
  • safe generated and public payload structure; and
  • the paths and capabilities of its own mutations.

It does not become the business-data validator for every application named by a document relationship. A cross-application identity may no longer resolve, and that state does not by itself invalidate the document or block publication.

Semantic Tokens already follows this pattern. Authoring validates a selected target at insertion, while rebuilding is tolerant: an unresolved occurrence does not block the document build, and diagnosis belongs to Docs Broken Links rather than a synchronization process.

Tag-document linking uses the complementary direction. A tag stores a one-way doc_id, while the document carries no tag back-reference. Either side may be deleted independently, leaving an unreferenced document or a stale registry identity.

Consequences For Collection Management

A Docs Viewer collection must manage its documents on their own terms:

  • list every locally manageable document, including unreferenced and non-viewable documents;
  • use Docs metadata such as title, Status, and visibility rather than copying Studio fields into the collection index;
  • allow exact document edits and deletions without consulting an external canonical owner;
  • preserve stale external relationships as diagnosable states;
  • avoid background repair, cascading deletes, or inferred associations; and
  • keep public publication independent from local management metadata.

The collection may contain duplicate titles, independently authored documents, or documents with no external association. Those are valid document states, not evidence that the collection must be synchronized with another registry.

Invariants

  • One application does not become a write proxy for another merely because it consumed its canonical data at creation.
  • Every ongoing mutation has one canonical owner and one explicit write path.
  • Cross-application identities are references, not shared ownership.
  • Initial validation does not imply permanent referential integrity.
  • Stale or broken references are visible and repairable without blocking unrelated document management or publication.
  • Generated outputs remain derived even when their source was initially seeded from another canonical system.
  • Public readers receive only the projection required for reading; they do not receive canonical Studio data or local repair capability.

Non-Goals

  • bidirectional synchronization;
  • automatic propagation of edits or deletes;
  • a cross-application transaction bus;
  • inferred matching by mutable labels or content;
  • background stale-reference repair;
  • copying complete Studio records into Docs Viewer; or
  • making Docs Viewer responsible for validating Studio's domain semantics.

The Sub-Scope Index feature applies this concept to generic collection navigation and management.
